decisions.reason: The reworded feedback describes the already-current $5 and $500-ticket allocation to a random existing NFT holder; it does not change the underlying no-code reward rule.
The source changes the invalid/no-code feedback text, not which referral codes are valid or the self-referral rule.
The badge-layout request is a separate clause in the same message and is unrelated to the source feedback-text modification.
The NFT-sizing approval is a separate observation and the referral-feedback wording change does not alter media display requirements.
The source requests exact wording for a validation popup, not a change to FAQ content; the underlying no-code allocation already matches the FAQ state.
The feedback-text revision does not change the use, permanence, or display locations of NFT mint numbers as referral codes.
Random allocation of a no-code referral reward to an existing NFT holder is distinct from selection of prize-draw winners and does not change that mechanism.
The popup wording change does not alter which counters, badges, or referral identifiers must appear in NFT metadata.
The source concerns no-code or invalid-code handling and does not change rewards for a successful coded referral.
The revised validation message does not change dashboard display or accounting of commissions and prize tickets.
The first-mint failure reported elsewhere in the same message is not part of the source wording modification, which does not change the USDC mint-flow requirement.
The feedback rewording identifies where a no-code ticket goes but does not change ticket counters, eligibility windows, expiration, or post-draw handling.
